label: Diagram 1.13
caption: Diagram 1.13 | Handrail design Guarding of stairs For all buildings
description: The drawing, captioned "Diagram 1.13 Handrail design", carries the note "See para 1.36" at the top left and has an upper and a lower part. The upper part is a side section showing two handrail cross-sections; the left one is connected to a bracket fixed to a hatched vertical wall on the left by a horizontal tube, and the right one is connected to a similar horizontal tube that stops short of the wall. The left form is a circle, labelled "Circular handrail 32mm to 50mm diameter"; a horizontal dimension from the wall to its near side reads "50mm to 75mm". The right form is an oval with a dashed inner curve on its left side, labelled "Non-circular handrail 50mm wide and 39mm deep having rounded edges", with a dimension to that curve reading "15mm min. radius". A vertical dimension between the underside of the handrail and the supporting horizontal tube reads "50mm min.". The lower part is a side section of a single post topped by a circle, set on a hatched horizontal surface whose right edge is indicated by an arrow labelled "Ramped or stepped access". A vertical dimension from the surface to the underside of the circle reads "50mm min.", and a horizontal dimension from the near side of the circle to the surface edge reads "50mm max."
